name: Photo library, full access
plain: Reads and edits every photo and video in the shared library.
meaning: Exposes the whole camera roll: faces, places (EXIF GPS), screenshots of IDs and bank pages, dates that map out a life. Apps rarely need all of it.

android.permission: READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO (API 33); READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE up to API 32
android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow per media type; Android 14 adds Select photos and videos
android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset after months unused (Android 11+)
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Photos and videos
android.store_policy: Play: broad photo and video access policy (2024) limits it to apps whose core function needs it
android.note: Android 10 scoped storage hid other apps' files; GPS in EXIF needs ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION

ios.prompt_ui: Select Photos, Allow Access to All Photos, Don't Allow (iOS 14+)
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1(ii): purpose string must explain use; missing key crashes the app
ios.note: Without the key the first PhotoKit call terminates the app

limits.headline: Can see and change every photo and video in your library once you allow full access
limits.user_action: You tap Allow access to all photos or Allow all, often for backup or editing
can: List and open every photo and video
Upload your whole library for backup or sync
Edit photos and save new versions
cannot: Open other apps' private folders on Android 10 and newer
See photo locations on Android without the separate media location permission
Skip the permission on iPhone; the app stops without the right setting
Keep access after you turn it off in Settings
limits.differs: Android 14 and iPhone iOS 14 both let you pick only some photos. Older Android is all or nothing per media type.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app read and change every photo and video in your library.
story.for_you: A pop up asks to access all photos. If you allow full access, the app can see every picture and video, including faces, places and screenshots of IDs and bank pages.
story.for_makers: Needed by apps that manage a whole library, like backup or cleaning tools. Most apps do not need all of it, and both platforms now push them toward pickers.

use_cases.example: A cloud backup app uploads every new photo to your account.
A photo editor shows your whole library and edits any picture.
A cleaner app finds duplicates and blurry shots to delete.
A memories app builds a slideshow from your year of photos.
A bad app might scan for pictures of IDs or cards.
A family album app shows kid photos to grandparents.
An ad firm could use photos to guess interests if an app shared them.

story.android_note: Needs READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO, and Play restricts it.
story.ios_note: Full access gives read and write to the entire library.

technical_bounds: Both platforms now let the user narrow the grant to chosen items
Apps that only need to pick a file are steered to the system picker

history.change: Limited library added; apps using the old call get .authorized for a limited grant
READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE replaced by granular media permissions
